A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAXO method and DET-COMPASS benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments across six X-ray datasets, comparisons with OVXD, component ablations and sensitivity analyses, with additional results and standard deviations in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LaMI-DETR evaluations, component replacement ablations, per-category results and computational timings.

M1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3, Equations 1–6 and Algorithm 1 retain the same retrieval, material-transfer, descriptor construction and classification procedures, including DCC. The component substitutions in new Table 10 are ablation variants rather than revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six X-ray detection datasets: DET-COMPASS, PIXray, PIDray, CLCXray, DvXray and HiXray. The new diagnostics reuse existing coverage; no new task, population or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 adds LaMI-DETR, evaluated both alone and with RAXO across the six datasets and five gallery compositions in Table 9. Existing detector comparisons, OVXD comparisons and the StyleShot comparator are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 10 adds controlled PIXray experiments under the 50/50 gallery setting, removing segmentation or the LLM and substituting SAM, LLaMA-3 or DINO. Existing CMTE protocols, metrics, gallery settings and default hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens diagnostic analysis: Tables 6–7 examine category-specific performance, Table 10 tests dependence on pretrained components, and Figure 9 visually compares material transfer with diffusion. Appendix C also adds class-distribution analysis, and D.6 adds computational-cost analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions already report three random in-house/web category assignments and standard deviations for intermediate gallery settings. These practices and values are retained in v1 Table 6, renumbered Table 8 in v2; no changed run count or uncertainty procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for LaMI-DETR, component variants and individual categories, plus timings and distribution statistics. For example, new Table 10 reports 25.4 AP for full RAXO versus 20.8 without the LLM; Table 6 reveals Bat scores of 70.7 for G-DINO and 69.7 with RAXO.

T1.justification: Appendix D.6 newly states O(n) inference complexity with respect to category count, a limited mathematical claim without a supporting derivation. The original mathematical formulation, equations and algorithm remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free adaptation of RGB detectors to X-ray, the DET-COMPASS benchmark and improvements of up to 17.0 average AP points. Added appendix evidence supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets stronger performance on distinctive shapes or cross-modal color shifts and difficulty with generic shapes. D.5 explains why scanner palette differences supposedly require no color adjustment, while Appendix E discusses replacing large components to balance efficiency and accuracy.

D1.justification: D.5–D.6 newly disclose the absence of cross-dataset color adjustments, DET-COMPASS raw density values, NVIDIA A100 hardware, approximately 0.7 seconds per class for descriptor construction and 3 milliseconds per sample overhead. The abstract also changes the resource link from a repository to a project website.

R1.justification: v2 adds the LaMI-DETR reference and positions its evaluation as validation with an LLM-guided DETR. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous X-ray detection approaches otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is retained with limited capitalization, cross-reference, corresponding-author and acknowledgement edits. The appendix gains explanatory subsections and reorganizes its analysis sections, moving the existing qualitative discussion from F to H without substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands appendix displays with per-category Tables 6–7, LaMI-DETR Table 9, component-ablation Table 10 and a new RGB/diffusion/material-transfer/ground-truth comparison in Figure 9. Existing displays are retained and reflowed or renumbered, including the original qualitative Figure 9 becoming Figure 10.

improvement.justification: The added appendix evidence strengthens checks of detector portability and component dependence, exposes category-specific weaknesses, and clarifies preprocessing and computational cost. These provide useful incremental improvements to v1's already extensive evaluation. The claimed efficiency tradeoff remains only partly demonstrated because the component variants report accuracy without corresponding runtime comparisons.
